Jack / Dylan / team — hi, Marissa from Privacy & InfoSec. Below are concise answers and references; weve attached a CSV mapping (oxbridge_transfer_map_questionnaire-resp.csv) and an SCC/DPF supplement doc.

1) Transfer mechanisms:
- Primary: Standard Contractual Clauses (EU SCCs) embedded in our DPA annex for EU -> US processing.
- Secondary: We support adherence to the EU-US Data Privacy Framework (DPF) where customers require DPF-specific attestations; operationally we maintain the policies and recordkeeping necessary for DPF certification renewals.
- Fallbacks: In limited cases where neither SCCs nor DPF are requested, we discuss narrow derogation clauses with legal teams; we do not rely on broad derogations for recurring processing.

2) DPA annex and mapping:
- The attached DPA annex v2 includes an exhibit mapping cross-border flows at the dataset/class level (PII / Sensitive Health / Identifiers).
- We can provide field-level mappings on a per-contract basis; that requires a brief technical intake to enumerate dataset schemas.

3) Technical controls (summary):
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ enforced for all endpoints; mTLS for dedicated/private deployments when requested.
- At-rest: AES-256; customer-specific keys via KMS available for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted customers, we offer managed KMS with tenant separation; bring-your-own-key (BYOK) is available for customers on our Dedicated or Private plans.
- KV cache & prompt handling: transient KV caches are strictly ephemeral per-request; cached prefixes used only to increase throughput are isolated by customer namespace and encrypted with the same KMS keys as persistent stores. Cache eviction is deterministic and tied to session lifecycle.
- Key separation: logical separation of keys by tenant for Dedicated and Private; hosted uses scoped keys with tenant access controls.
- Access controls: role-based access control (RBAC), just-in-time privileged sessions for infra ops, and audit logging for administrative access.

4) Sub-processors and notification:
- We maintain a living sub-processor registry (included in the CSV) and notify customers of material changes 30 days before onboarding new sub-processors. For critical regions, we support sub-processor reviews under an NDA.

5) Retention & deletion propagation:
- Customer-initiated deletion: we commit to propagating deletion to live caches, model feature stores, and backups per agreed SLAs. For hosted customers, deletion requests trigger: immediate removal from KV cache, background purge jobs for persistent stores (within 72 hours for most artifacts), and audit log entries documenting operations.
- We document deletion workflows in the DPA annex; physical destruction policies and retention schedules are available on request.

Attachments: oxbridge_transfer_map_questionnaire-resp.csv; sccs-supplement-2026.docx

If you want field-level mappings, please share a representative schema and Ill have the tech privacy analyst produce the export. Happy to jump on a call to walk through the CSV.

Best,

Jack — hi, Mina from InfoSec and Controls. Per Marissas note, here are short paragraph summaries for procurement: 

1) Audit log retention: We retain tamper-evident administrative and audit logs for a minimum of 12 months for hosted and Dedicated customers. Logs are stored in immutable object storage with write-once retention controls and cryptographic integrity checks. Access to log retrieval is limited via RBAC and requires an approved incident/forensic request with auditable approvals.

2) Hosted customer KMS separation and operator access: For hosted customers that opt for managed KMS, keys are created in a tenant-scoped key namespace; platform operations access requires a documented escalation and is subject to just-in-time privilege elevation with multi-person approval. Key material is never exposed in plaintext to platform ops; operations run against ciphertext via controlled KMS APIs. Dedicated/Private customers can use BYOK where Redwood does not hold key material.

3) Deletion propagation SLA summary: Customer deletion requests trigger immediate eviction from in-memory and KV caches and schedule background deletion from persistent stores and backups. Typical timeline: cache eviction immediate, persistent store purge within 72 hours, verification log entry within 7 days. Specific SLA windows are contractible in the DPA annex.

If you want these consolidated into a short PDF or added to the DPA annex preamble, we can attach it to the signature package.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
